verdict.rationale: Cloudflare publishes a public SFU pricing page that meters bandwidth in GB. It states that the first 1,000 GB each month is free, that ingress (published traffic) is free, and that TURN is free when used with the SFU, so a founder can begin modeling cost without sales contact. However, the evidence never quotes the actual per-GB rate beyond the free tier, and gives no per-participant-minute pricing for RealtimeKit. Missing for 10: the published per-GB egress rate after the free 1,000 GB, RealtimeKit per-participant-minute or recording/transcription rates, and independent confirmation that the cost modeling works in practice.

support.subject: As a founder, usage pricing is published per participant-minute or per unit of bandwidth, so I can model cost without talking to sales

citations.quote: The first 1,000 GB each month is free.
Traffic published into Cloudflare is free, including when no client subscribes to that publication.
Using Cloudflare Realtime TURN service is available free of charge when used together with the Realtime SFU.
